description: Meta's largest data-center campus, a 5 GW AI supercluster under construction in Richland Parish, Louisiana, with investment now above $50B. Financed partly through a record $27B private-credit joint venture with Blue Owl Capital (Blue Owl funds own 80%, Meta 20%); first 2 GW targeted by 2030, full build ~2032.

Power-infrastructure developer behind the 1,000-acre Lancium Clean Campus in Abilene, Texas — the first operational site of the Stargate AI data-center initiative (SoftBank/OpenAI/Oracle). Backed by Blackstone; NVIDIA is reported to be investing $2B for roughly 20% (up to $3B total) at a ~$10B valuation, with a possible 2027 IPO.

Jeff Bezos's space company (founded 2000): New Glenn heavy-lift rockets, BE-4 engines, the Blue Moon lunar lander and New Shepard suborbital flights. In July 2026 it raised its first-ever outside round — about $10B at a $130B valuation — with Bezos putting in $2B alongside ~$4B from Coatue; Bezos had previously funded it with roughly $30B.

San Francisco software-first critical-minerals company (CEO Turner Caldwell) that engineers, builds and operates mines and refineries on its MarianaOS platform; flagship sites include Copper One in southeastern Utah and Lithium One in East Texas. Raised a $310M Series B led by Khosla Ventures with a16z, Breakthrough Energy, BHP Ventures and In-Q-Tel — ~$400M raised to date.

ASX-listed critical-minerals developer (SRL, Melbourne; backed by Robert Friedland) behind the 100%-owned Syerston Scandium Project in New South Wales, designed to produce ~60 tonnes of scandium a year for aerospace-grade aluminum alloys. The US Department of War's Office of Strategic Capital signed a conditional commitment of up to US$400M in long-term debt for the project; the company is also pursuing a US listing.

Minneapolis-area company commercializing rare-earth-free Iron Nitride permanent magnets, based on technology developed at the University of Minnesota. The US Department of War's Office of Strategic Capital signed a conditional 20-year loan commitment of up to $150M to fund its 287,000 sq ft Sartell, Minnesota plant, slated to produce up to 1,500 tons of magnets annually from 2027.

Refractory-grade bauxite supplier named 'Standard Bauxite' in the White House fact sheet; the Department of War release identifies the counterparty as Strategic Bauxite USA, LLC (SBX), which acquired Canada's First Bauxite Corporation. The DoW's $85.5M IBAS equity investment (plus $64.5M private co-investment) funds expansion of the First Bauxite mine in Guyana, calcination facilities, and a US brown-fused alumina plant.

AI infrastructure company (founded 2024, CEO Vincent Weisser) building an open 'superintelligence stack' — GPU compute, reinforcement-learning frameworks and evals that let enterprises train and run their own AI models and agents instead of relying on frontier labs. Raised a $130M Series A at a $1B valuation led by Radical Ventures, with NVIDIA Ventures, Intel Capital and Dell Technologies Capital; ~$100M revenue run rate.

Riyadh-based enterprise AI company focused on financial-crime prevention and decision intelligence; its FOCAL platform (AML/KYC) serves 150+ financial-services and public-sector customers across the Middle East. Received a strategic investment from HUMAIN (Saudi PIF's AI company) — HUMAIN Ventures' first investment in a Saudi company — paired with a partnership to co-build enterprise AI solutions.

Public benefit corporation founded in August 2026 by Google veterans Jeff Dean (CEO), Sanjay Ghemawat, Oriol Vinyals and Quoc Le to use AI to automate large-scale scientific and engineering experimentation. Seed round co-led by Radical Ventures and Khosla Ventures, with Alphabet participating as founding investor and cloud partner alongside Lightspeed and Kleiner Perkins.
